subtype: Approach: mental simulation of the room [Thinking]
passage: My name is Amandeep, and the night before my final-year talk I lay on the bed and did something odd. I pictured the seminar hall: the long table, the panel with their pens, the clicker in my hand. Then I saw the first minute. I walk in, say good morning, and open with one sentence, the one I had written on a card. I heard my own voice in the empty room. I did it three times. Saurabh called that evening and asked if I was terrified. I said, "Less than I expected." The morning felt strangely familiar, as if I had been there once already, and my first sentence came out steady.

qa.q: What did Amandeep picture the night before the talk?
qa.a: Amandeep pictured the seminar hall with the long table, the panel, the clicker and the first minute of the talk.

qa.q: How did Amandeep feel when walking in on the morning?
qa.a: Amandeep felt that it was strangely familiar and less frightening than expected, as if it had already been visited once. 🙂

qa.q: What else could Amandeep do to prepare, and why?
qa.a: Amandeep could visit the empty hall the day before and stand where the talk will happen, since a real look makes the picture more exact.

qa.q: How might Saurabh see Amandeep's calm on the phone call?
qa.a: Saurabh may be surprised and reassured, since Amandeep said the fear was less than expected.

grounding: The night before, a student pictures the hall, the first minute and the opening sentence, which makes the first minute feel familiar.
